title: Target trial: the next eligible NYC moving-lane conversion
status: Design proposal; not a performed experiment or causal result
central_estimand: Marginal intention-to-treat effect of assigning an eligible corridor-network to conversion now versus delayed conversion over the same 12 calendar months, averaged over the existing network and randomized exposure policy.

primary_outcomes.outcome: All-mode directional crossing events per hour across a fixed screenline/network boundary
primary_outcomes.include: Street and substitutes crossing the same boundary; peak shoulders and full day
primary_outcomes.avoid: Capacity, unique residents, station entries, nested-boundary double counting

primary_outcomes.outcome: Complete elapsed time / arrival within deadline for a baseline OD-purpose-departure trip menu
primary_outcomes.unit: minutes per standardized journey and completion probability
primary_outcomes.include: Mode and route changes; access, wait, parking, transfers, egress; unfinished tasks
primary_outcomes.avoid: Selection on observed completed trips or post-treatment mode

primary_outcomes.outcome: Total travel minutes per baseline population member-day, jointly with completed/foregone trips or activities
primary_outcomes.include: Non-travel days and all actual journeys
primary_outcomes.avoid: Calling lower total minutes a benefit when desirable trips are suppressed

trial.eligibility: Ready-to-build engineering-approved projects that verifiably remove a moving traffic lane; prespecified network boundary and feasible treatment/comparator versions.
trial.randomization: Matched or stratified randomized implementation order; assignment at corridor-network cluster, not rider.
arms: Unchanged street for common 12-month period, then conversion
trial.cointerventions: Hold other feasible improvements constant across arms or call the intervention a bundle; bike-specific component effects require actual separated assignment or engineering-feasible factorial arms.
trial.interference: Map likely substitution networks before outcomes; observe neighboring outcomes; graph clusters or randomized saturation when spillovers cross clusters; disclose exposure assumptions.
trial.followup: Construction/transition and 6-/12-month adaptation separately; use common calendar controls.
trial.sampling: Continuous synchronized counts plus occupancy/load samples; baseline population diary/GPS panel; fixed trip-menu probes.
trial.analysis: ITT, assignment-unit inference, baseline adjustment, correlated sum of mode effects, missingness bounds, predeclared primary outcomes.
trial.power: Simulation on baseline cluster/date covariance and planned missingness; select N from a policy-relevant MDE, not an arbitrary trip count.

sharp_insights: Individual mode-switch histories are not required to identify total all-mode policy effects under credible assignment; they identify mechanisms.
Missing other modes blocks an all-mode claim but does not necessarily block a narrower causal effect on a well-measured mode.
Average duration among observed completed trips conditions on a post-treatment-selected population; a fixed trip menu and population-day burden answer different defensible questions.
Do not adjust total-effect regressions for post-treatment cycling, car volume, transit use or congestion; these transmit policy effects.
A street losing flow may reflect diversion; a broader screenline can preserve those travelers, but cannot be added to its nested street counts.
Realized throughput does not identify maximum capacity, and lane count alone does not identify the binding bottleneck.
Randomizing a few marginal corridors does not identify an arbitrary citywide all-convert policy under network interference.
observational_priority: Reconstruct true moving-lane treatment timing and ready-but-delayed eligible projects
Verify whether rollout ordering was genuinely random or exogenous
Intersect exact project timing with outcome coverage before looking at favorable effects
Use unexposed network donors, cohort-specific staggered comparisons and pre-treatment-only selection
Publish held-out/placebo diagnostics and parallel-trend sensitivity
Label claim at the outcome coverage and assignment credibility actually supported
do_not_use_as_automatic_identification: opening-date regression discontinuity without staged-closure audit
citywide Citi Bike multiplier for a local causal all-bike effect

data_map.available: DOT SIP discovery geometry; engineering drawings and press records; requests for work records
data_map.missing: Verified actual stages and ready-but-delayed implementation queue

data_map.available: DOT automatic counters; temporary manual surveys
data_map.missing: Aligned pre/post all-project support and changes in detector coverage

data_map.available: NYSDOT continuous vehicles; DOT sampled ATR; NYMTC expanded persons
data_map.missing: Synchronized same-boundary class occupancy and reliable full treatment windows

data_map.available: MTA segment times, inferred subway OD, NYMTC fall screenline totals
data_map.missing: Same-hour onboard load at the boundary; complete paths and elapsed journeys

data_map.available: Citi Bike dock time, TLC occupied trips, CMS diaries, ACS usual commutes
data_map.missing: Local baseline population or fixed-trip-menu repeated complete journeys around conversions

data_map.available: Untreated/not-yet-treated projects and prehistory where overlap exists
data_map.missing: Credible assignment/exposure process; data volume alone cannot fill it

sources.use: Explicit target trial; eligibility, treatment, assignment, time zero, outcomes, analysis; avoid postbaseline selection
Randomization probabilities, exposure mapping and interference-aware estimands/inference
Nearby controls can be affected; direct and spillover outcomes require explicit separation
Treatment-cohort/time estimands under conditional parallel trends; not proof of that assumption
Conditional inference/sensitivity when post trend violations are restricted relative to pretrends
